💧 A woman, maybe 50s, with a burn-scarred forearm returns with water: +3 clean.
A woman, maybe 50s, with a burn-scarred forearm shakes their head. "Ask someone who trusts you." (Trust too low.)
"Can we talk?" A woman, maybe 50s, with a burn-scarred forearm sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to." (Talk to A woman, maybe 50s, with a burn-scarred forearm.)
A woman, maybe 50s, with a burn-scarred forearm hesitates, then backs off. "Not today. Sorry." (Low trust — reluctant.)
You catch fragments by the fire — A woman, maybe 50s, with a burn-scarred forearm telling Ethan about you. The story's getting bigger than what happened.

A woman, maybe 50s, with a burn-scarred forearm spends the afternoon with the small tree with mitten-shaped leaves (three shapes), spicy root smell — look, smell, the smallest taste, then waiting. By evening a woman, maybe 50s, with a burn-scarred forearm is thoroughly, educationally sick. "NOT food," they announce to the fire, pale. "My body told me so." The lesson is learned the hard way — and now the whole village knows it.
💡 The small tree with mitten-shaped leaves (three shapes), spicy root smell — THAT's what A woman, maybe 50s, with a burn-scarred forearm was describing. Sassafras. It clicks like a key turning.

A woman, maybe 50s, with a burn-scarred forearm spends the afternoon with the vine with thick-skinned round fruit — look, smell, the smallest taste, then waiting. An hour passes. Then another. Nothing. The fire nods. That's dinner, maybe.
the woman in her 50s, with a burn-scarred forearm spent the afternoon at the workbench and made 5 Arrow — and carries them now, their own work in their own hands.

You catch fragments by the fire — A woman, maybe 50s, with a burn-scarred forearm telling A woman, maybe 30s about herself. Three retellings in, nobody remembers what actually happened — but everyone has opinions.
A woman, maybe 50s, with a burn-scarred forearm is sweeping the hall. Someone has to.
You catch fragments by the fire — Austin telling A woman, maybe 50s, with a burn-scarred forearm about Ethan. The truth left this story two fires ago. What's left is better theater.

A woman, maybe 50s, with a burn-scarred forearm spends the afternoon with the thorny bush with dark berries — look, smell, the smallest taste, then waiting. An hour passes. Then another. Nothing. The fire nods. That's dinner, maybe.
💡 The thorny bush with dark berries — THAT's what A woman, maybe 50s, with a burn-scarred forearm was describing. Blackberry. It clicks like a key turning.
A person, maybe 30s, with a buzz cut showed A woman, maybe 50s, with a burn-scarred forearm the Spicebush — "remember it." The haven hears about it by supper.
A woman, maybe 50s, with a burn-scarred forearm will work the garden once each day while at Haven. Other orders take priority.

Fireside lesson: A woman, maybe 50s, with a burn-scarred forearm passes around Sassafras. Someone asks a dumb question. Nobody minds. That's how you learn.

A woman, maybe 50s, with a burn-scarred forearm spends the afternoon with the tree with lobed leaves and oval nuts in scaly caps — look, smell, the smallest taste, then waiting. Raw, it knots the stomach. Cooked... fine. The fire learns the rule before the name: cook it, or else.
The Journal notes it: White Oak Acorns — cook it, or else. (A woman, maybe 50s, with a burn-scarred forearm tested it.)
🌱 A woman, maybe 50s, with a burn-scarred forearm waters and weeds the beds before taking up other work. The harvest can wait.

🌿 A woman, maybe 50s, with a burn-scarred forearm checks the pantry before heading out — the shelves are full, ~11 days of fresh on hand… leaves the harvest standing and turns to the wood run instead. The pantry can't take more; the wild will keep.
🪵 A woman, maybe 50s, with a burn-scarred forearm hauls back 5 wood. The pile grows. (48 logs now.)
A woman, maybe 50s, with a burn-scarred forearm is stitching a tear shut by the door light, squinting at every stitch. The pantry won't fill itself.
